examples.label: Fingerprint kernel + sudo to pick a CVE
Near-universal / modern picks
examples.command: # PwnKit CVE-2021-4034 (polkit, almost any distro) | Dirty Pipe CVE-2022-0847 (kernel 5.8-5.17)

notes:
Sudo:
  CVE-2021-3156 (Baron Samedit)  sudo <= 1.9.5p1 (1.8.31/1.8.27/1.9.2)
  CVE-2019-14287 (neg UID)        sudo < 1.8.28, needs (ALL,!root) rule
Polkit:
  CVE-2021-4034 (PwnKit)          any system with SUID pkexec (12+ yrs)
Kernel:
  CVE-2016-5195 (DirtyCow)        old kernels
  CVE-2022-0847 (Dirty Pipe)      5.8 - 5.17
  CVE-2021-22555 (netfilter)      2.6 - 5.11
  CVE-2022-25636 (netfilter)      5.4 - 5.6.10
  CVE-2023-32233 (netfilter)      up to 6.3.1

recommended.note: PwnKit is the safest near-universal pick.

name: Reference - Linux Local-Root CVE Quick-Pick
command: uname -r; sudo -V | head -n1   # then match against this list
description: Fast lookup mapping kernel/sudo/polkit versions to a known local-root exploit - the first thing to check on a Linux target.
